notes.title: 2025 Plans
notes.content:
Hi Everyone,

I'd like to announce a preview of things to come to [b]Hotel: Collector's Edition[/b]:

For the past 2 years we've been slowly working on porting our old engine to modern platforms.
In the process of doing so, we released one of the games we made using the same engine that has been used for the Hotel: Collector's Edition. The game is a platformer game for kids, called [b]"Tibor: Tale of a Kind Vampire"[/b], which was originally released in 2009.
Check it out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3285420/Tibor_Tale_of_a_Kind_Vampire/][b]here[/b][/url].

These games were made using 'Python' and 'Ogre3D engine' and now the old games run inside our newer engine which we use for most of our other games. Think of it as a sort of a 'virtual machine' for older games.

What this means in short term is that we are planning to port Hotel: Collector's Edition to this new engine. This will immediately bring the following benefits:
[list]
[*]The game's 3D models will look much sharper and will be anti-aliased, (no more hard edges)
[*]The game will work on MacOS and Linux
[/list]

Currently, Windows players have the option to play either the old "Hotel: Collector's Edition" or the newer casual version "Brightstone Mysteries: Hotel", while MacOS and Linux players currently have only the latter.
With these changes, both MacOS and Linux players will be able to play both versions.
Depending on technical issues, these 2 versions will either be separate games you can choose to launch in Steam, or (hopefully) we'll be able to integrate both versions in one game.

Then you could choose the game mode from within the game:
The old "hardcore" version with a 3d character or the newer "casual" version without a movable character but with integrated hints and other modern goodies.


This is just the beginning, the first step in a larger journey of remastering Hotel: Collector's Edition. We have more plans to improve this game in 2025, stay tuned. 🙂

All of these upgrades, like the previous ones - are coming to you as a free update, no DLC and no "Deluxe" or "Remastered" Edition.

notes.title: Linux version now available!
notes.content:
We're happy to announce we've released the Linux version of Hotel Collector's Edition!

As far as our games are concerned, Linux is no longer a "second-class citizen", we're rolling out Linux support for ALL games in our catalogue and we will continue to support our games on all 3 major Steam platforms with updates from now on.

Everything works nicely, we tested the game on many Linux distributions as well as Steam Deck.
We built the game for Linux according to Steam developer guidelines so we don't expect much problems, but if you do encounter issues, please write in the Discussion forum and we'll investigate.

Also, if you play this game on Linux and everything works, we'd still love to hear from you and know which Distro/CPU/GPU you use.

PS: As with the Mac version, the Linux version contains only the casual version of the game "Brightstone Mysteries: Paranormal Hotel".

We do have plans to bring the old point and click version with a movable character to Mac and Linux as well, but since that version is done in a different engine, it's rather difficult to port it to Mac and Linux.
If you prefer the original version and would like tho play on Linux or Steam Deck, until then, you can play the game using Proton compatibility layer.

notes.title: Remastered / Casual versions explained
notes.content:
Remastered / Casual versions explained
Starting August 4th, 2023, you'll see 2 versions of the game when you press play:

Casual Remastered version
Legacy Point and Click version

The "legacy" version is the original game, which is a traditional point and click adventure game, with a movable 3d character on a 2d background.
It is limited to 4:3 aspect ratio and comes only in English and German (full audio with voice acting for German version)

The "casual" version was released in 2013, which has many improvements, but does not have a traditional movable character you would expect a point and click game to have.

The most important improvements the casual version has over the legacy one are as follows:
Widescreen support
More crisp graphics
Interactive hint system
Skip-able mini-games
Support for steam achievements
Support for steam cloud saves

Notes:
The legacy version does not support Steam cloud or Steam achievements!
The Legacy version is only available on Windows. We have some plans to bring it to MacOS and Linux as well, but it's hard to say when or if we'll be able to do that, due to the technical limitations of the engine used in the old version of the game.
Thus, on MacOS, you can only play the Casual version.

And as always, let us know if you have any technical problems playing the game and we'll do our best to fix them asap.
And last but not least, just because the new version is not out, does not mean we'll stop supporting the Legacy version. If you run into trouble, please report it in the forums and we'll check it out.
